clue.text: Surprise misfortune

parts.note: an unexpected blow that knocks progress backwards, read as a plain description

explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of fortune, often coming without warning, which is what a surprise misfortune is.

clue.text: A bluebird? No! One in exaltation

definitions.text: A bluebird? No! One in exaltation

parts.words: A bluebird? No! One in exaltation
parts.note: the bird belongs to the blue heavens, and 'an exaltation' is the collective noun for a flock of these songbirds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exaltation' looks like joy, but it is the traditional collective noun for larks; the bird is 'blue' because it soars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird sings high in the sky, and a group of them is called an exaltation.

clue.text: Hard drudgery could be mild later

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a hard grind now might become gentler later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' tells you to rearrange MILD LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any monotonous, wearying routine of hard work.

clue.text: Computer used in the Hickstead Derby

indicators.note: the answer is found lying inside the run of the next words

explanation.surface: A computer was employed at a famous show-jumping event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hickstead Derby is a famous English show-jumping competition; the answer sits across 'HicksteAD DERby'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adds up figures computes, so an adding machine is a computer in the old sense.

clue.text: He once recruited someone to work for the Aga

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., the British war minister whose pointing face on a poster recruited soldiers in the First World War

definitions.text: someone to work for the Aga
definitions.meaning: an Aga is a British range cooker, so one working at it is a cook's helper in the kitchen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Aga' looks like an Ottoman commander, but it is the cast-iron cooker found in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener led the famous recruiting campaign; a kitchener is also a person employed in a kitchen.

clue.text: Strong stem …

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood from a wound

explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is a strong one, and to staunch bleeding is to stem it.

clue.text: These letters can appear in paper

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the word given may show up in a different order

explanation.surface: A note that certain letters may turn up printed on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can appear' tells you to rearrange THESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single piece of paper.

clue.text: A Lima lord battling for this protected species

indicators.note: a fight throws the letters into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Peruvian aristocrat fights to save an endangered animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima is the capital of Peru; 'battling' tells you to rearrange A LIMA LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal, protected by its bony plates and in places by law.

clue.text: Alan's manufactured part of helmet

indicators.note: made up anew, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man named Alan has made a component for a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' tells you to rearrange ALANS; the 's is counted as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The nasal is the nose-guard bar on a medieval helmet.

clue.text: A home economist?

parts.note: the verb meaning to manage resources thriftily is also the word for the man of the house

explanation.walkthrough: To husband resources is to use them sparingly, so the married man of the household can be pictured as a domestic economiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a man in a home, and to husband is to economise, hence a home economist.

clue.text: … part with fruit

definitions.meaning: the crop or produce of the land

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 5 Across in the surface only; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give up something, and a yield is also a harvest or crop.

clue.text: When the Russian lawgiver appears, they can keep cool

parts.note: taken as written
R is a standard abbreviation for Russian
Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai

explanation.surface: Whenever a Russian lawmaker turns up, people stay calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuum flasks keep drinks cold as well as hot.

clue.text: Trees burning at military base

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: Trees are on fire at an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a town in Hampshire, England, long known as the home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is the garrison town regarded as the home of the British Army.

clue.text: Cook greeted at Wapping on return

indicators.note: signals that the word is read backwards

parts.note: Wapping is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H, so hailed becomes 'ailed

explanation.surface: A chef was welcomed back at a London riverside district.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is the best-known British cookery writer and TV chef.

clue.text: Killer's in a dive when after Jack

definitions.meaning: a blade that kills, with 's read as is

definitions.text: in a dive when after Jack
definitions.meaning: a jack-... is a dive in which the body folds and opens

explanation.walkthrough: The jack-knife is a diving move, so the answer is what follows 'Jack' in the name of that dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a lethal weapon, and it completes the name of the jack-knife dive.

clue.text: A helper worried about me only for one day?

indicators.note: says one part goes around another
worried here means disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An assistant is anxious about me, perhaps only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes EPHERAL from A HELPER, and 'about' puts it around ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral comes from Greek for lasting a day, so it fits something lasting only one day.

clue.text: A nude told off for revealing lumps

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A naked person is told off for showing lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' tells you to rearrange A NUDE TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated means having nodules, small lumps, so it shows lumps.

clue.text: Breaker of secret recording failure

parts.note: a disc is a sound recording
a loser is a person who fails

explanation.surface: Someone leaks secrets about a recording that flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: One who discloses breaks a secret by revealing it.

clue.text: The fall of Niobe?

parts.note: in Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her children, so her 'fall' is the falling of her weeping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a downfall, but here it is the falling of what she wept.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobe was turned to stone and wept forever, so what fell from her were drops of weeping.

clue.text: Fish and chips cooked with lard

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into another form

explanation.surface: Fish and chips fried in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' tells you to rearrange CHIPS and LARD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilchards are small oily fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Call for a National Theatre show

parts.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager
NT is the abbreviation for the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a London theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public show or spectacle.

clue.text: Solar storm tests

indicators.note: a storm scatters things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solar storm is being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' tells you to rearrange SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Orals are spoken examinations.

clue.text: Dreamlike change in rural Southeast

indicators.note: a change in the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: Things look dreamlike after a change in rural southeast England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change in' tells you to rearrange RURAL together with SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes the strange, dreamlike quality of the Surrealist painters.

clue.text: Brilliance of a single amethyst

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: The sparkle of one purple gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'sinGLE AMethyst'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a flash or glint of light, a kind of brilliance.

clue.text: An apple taken off a tree

indicators.note: taken off as in copied or mimicked loosely, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An apple has been picked from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' tells you to rearrange A TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is an apple grown for eating raw rather than cooking.

clue.text: Dutchman giving shout within?

parts.note: a native of the Netherlands whose name holds a word for a loud shout broken open

explanation.walkthrough: The name contains HOLLER (shout) with AND inside it, which the question mark hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hollander is a person from Holland, a Dutchman.

clue.text: Dances round in rings

parts.note: hops are informal dances
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dancing round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside HOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoops are rings, such as those of a barrel.

clue.text: A fool switched to cold

indicators.note: switched around means the letters swap positions

explanation.surface: A clown turns frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched' tells you to rearrange A FOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and unfriendly, socially cold.

clue.text: Where to wait at the BBC when on air?

definitions.text: Where to wait at the BBC when on air?

parts.words: Where to wait at the BBC when on air?
parts.note: the BBC's nickname is Auntie, so its rooms spoken out loud suggest waiting rooms

explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is nicknamed 'Auntie'; 'Auntie rooms' sounds like the rooms where visitors wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterooms are small rooms leading to larger ones, used as waiting areas.

clue.text: Bracing air in Ohio district

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for the US state of Ohio
a zone is an area or district

explanation.surface: Fresh air in an area of the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly used for fresh, invigorating sea air.

clue.text: Creature mocked in the soup kitchen

definitions.text: Creature mocked in the soup kitchen

parts.words: Creature mocked in the soup kitchen
parts.note: mock soup imitates a shelled reptile, so the creature is 'mocked' in kitchens

explanation.walkthrough: Mock turtle soup was made with calf's head to imitate the real dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Turtles are shelled reptiles, imitated in the Victorian dish mock turtle soup.

clue.text: The jumper's way of saying "Neigh!"

parts.note: a show-jumping horse stopping at a fence says 'nay', which sounds like its neigh

explanation.walkthrough: The jumper is a horse, not a sweater; when it balks at a fence it is saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that stops at a jump makes a refusal, a declining to go over.
